name: OWASP Top 10 Client-Side Security Risks
source_notes: Candidate list and status verified on the owasp.org project page and its index.md (front-matter level 2, type documentation).
caveats: OWASP assigns no official prefix; CSn is reinhardt's local label for list position n. Cite as e.g. "OWASP Client-Side Top 10 (candidate) #6 JavaScript Drift".
Still a candidate list; the promised full draft (planned for later in 2022) never appeared, so the project is effectively stalled. No release or last-updated date.
Maturity 'incubator' is from front-matter level 2 and the page badge.
Prevention is [] because the list itself provides no countermeasures; related guidance lives in the Third Party JavaScript Management, HTML5 Security and CSP cheat sheets.
detection.static entries are reinhardt rule ideas, not OWASP text.

items.name: Broken Client-side Access Control
items.summary: JavaScript access to client-side data and code is not adequately controlled, enabling exfiltration or malicious DOM manipulation.

static: window.addEventListener('message', ...) handlers with no event.origin check
postMessage(data, '*')
Origin checks using indexOf / substring matching

items.name: DOM-based XSS
items.summary: DOM manipulation or abuse allows cross-site scripting.

static: innerHTML / outerHTML / insertAdjacentHTML / document.write / eval / new Function / setTimeout(string) fed from location, URLSearchParams or postMessage data
React dangerouslySetInnerHTML or Vue v-html with unsanitized input

items.name: Sensitive Data Leakage
items.summary: Trackers and pixels across a web property are not detected or controlled, risking privacy-law violations.

static: Third-party tracking pixels and tag-manager snippets (e.g. GTM gtm.js, Segment) whose downstream recipients are unknown
Tokens or PII in URL query strings that leak via Referer to third parties

items.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
items.summary: Outdated or known-vulnerable JavaScript libraries are not detected and updated.

static: Lockfile entries matching known-vulnerable library versions (RetireJS-style)

items.name: Lack of Third-party Origin Control
items.summary: Resources from third-party origins are not restricted according to their origin.

static: Third-party <script src="https://..."> includes
No CSP restricting script sources

items.name: JavaScript Drift
items.summary: Changes to client-side JavaScript assets and code are not detected.

static: Third-party scripts loaded from CDNs without integrity= (SRI) and crossorigin
Tag managers that can inject arbitrary scripts

items.name: Sensitive Data Stored Client-Side
items.summary: Sensitive data is kept in LocalStorage, the browser cache or transient JavaScript state.

static: localStorage/sessionStorage.setItem('token'|'jwt'|'session'|'access_token'|'refresh...', ...)
PII keys written to browser storage

items.name: Client-side Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
items.summary: Client-side changes and data access are not monitored or detected.

review: Requires runtime client-side monitoring; not statically detectable

items.name: Not Using Standard Browser Security Controls
items.summary: Standard browser controls such as CSP, Subresource Integrity and iframe sandboxing are not used.

static: Third-party <script>/<link> without integrity=
No CSP header/meta in framework config (next.config.js headers, vercel.json, helmet)
CSP containing 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval' or wildcard sources
iframes embedding untrusted content without sandbox

items.name: Including Proprietary Information on the Client-Side
items.summary: Sensitive business logic, developer comments, proprietary algorithms or system information ship to the client.

static: Production source maps (e.g. productionBrowserSourceMaps: true)
Secrets or private keys in NEXT_PUBLIC_* / VITE_* env vars
Developer comments shipped in bundles
